weekly_takeaways: Indonesia pledged to restructure its flagship Free Nutritious Meals program within one month amid mounting corruption allegations and budget inefficiencies. || Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz stranded two Indonesian Pertamina tankers as Jakarta offered to mediate between Washington and Tehran. || Parliament passed a controversial police law allowing active officers to hold civilian government posts and extending the retirement age.

Indonesia overhauled its flagship Free Nutritious Meals program mid-week amid corruption allegations, business operator backlash, and mounting student demonstrations. || The United States and Iran signed a preliminary peace deal on June 15 to end their three-month war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, though implementation quickly became contentious. || Coalition parties pressed PDI-P throughout the week to clarify whether it supports or opposes the Prabowo government, drawing sharp rebukes from the former ruling party.

Five candidates for Koperasi Desa Merah Putih manager positions died during military-style training between June 17 and 26. || A Bung Karno University student leader admitted receiving 20 million rupiah connected to a June 15 demonstration and meeting with Vice President Gibran. || Former President Jokowi launched a political safari in Lampung wearing PSI party regalia, drawing reactions from PDI-P to Gerindra.

Five trainees died during military drills for village cooperative managers, prompting Indonesia to scale back the program amid criticism it militarized civilian roles. || Former President Jokowi launched a political tour with PSI across Lampung and announced plans for Central Java, fueling speculation about the 2029 elections. || Papuan separatists shot and killed American pilot Nicholas Goselin and burned his aircraft on July 2, escalating conflict in Indonesia's restive highlands.

Indonesia sent Foreign Minister Sugiono to Iran's holy city of Mashhad to attend the burial of Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei amid escalating U.S.-Iran military strikes. || Indonesia and India signed a defense deal for BrahMos supersonic cruise missiles and Astra air-to-air missiles during Modi's state visit to Jakarta. || Prabowo inaugurated five dams across four provinces on Friday, projects the government expects to add one million tons of rice production annually.

President Prabowo authorized a comprehensive review of the flagship free nutritious meals program after partner associations threatened to shut down kitchens nationwide over governance disputes. || The United States and Iran exchanged intensifying strikes for eight consecutive nights after their June ceasefire collapsed over control of the Strait of Hormuz. || Parliamentary leaders sharply criticized civil servant work culture, prompting the minister to issue a public letter defending millions of government employees.

Nanik Deyang resigned as head of Indonesia's National Nutrition Agency after 44 days, citing heart treatment, and was replaced by former deputy agriculture minister Sudaryono. || Armed separatists in Papua's Yahukimo district killed three indigenous civilians on July 20, accusing them of intelligence work, and security forces evacuated two bodies by week's end. || Foreign Minister Sugiono pressed Japan and ASEAN partners to strengthen support for Palestine during a week of meetings in Manila tied to the 59th ASEAN ministerial summit.

Indonesia's Constitutional Court ruled that the flagship free nutritious meals program must be separated from the education budget by 2028. || President Prabowo's electability plunged from 34.9 percent to 14.5 percent over nine months, according to a survey released Thursday. || Kaesang Pangarep declared he would run for parliament from Central Java's fifth district in the 2029 elections.

Seventy-nine local governments face payroll shortfalls requiring Rp 3.7 trillion, prompting the central government to offer a three-step solution. || The Constitutional Court ruled that the Free Nutritious Meals program budget must be separated from the education allocation by 2028. || Indonesia cut first steel for its domestically-built Scorpene submarine at PT PAL's Surabaya shipyard on August 7.

President Prabowo proposed Destry Damayanti as sole candidate for Bank Indonesia governor and floated amnesty for SOE executives in his major annual address. || Celebrations marking 21 years of peace in Aceh descended into violence when crowds clashed with security forces over a crescent-star flag. || Indonesia's navy conducted a passing exercise with China near Taiwan, drawing condemnation from Taipei and requests for clarification.

Tensions erupted in Aceh on August 15 when a man replaced the Indonesian flag with a GAM-linked crescent flag during a peace anniversary event, triggering clashes and warning shots. || One Indonesian soldier died and two were wounded in a firefight with armed separatists in Papua's Mimika district during Independence Day celebrations. || Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and Defense Minister Dong Jun met President Prabowo on Friday following strategic talks focused on deepening bilateral cooperation.

DPR leadership pledged to pass the Asset Forfeiture Bill by December 15 after demonstrations on August 27 brought anti-corruption demands to parliament. || Indonesia's first aircraft carrier, the former Italian vessel Giuseppe Garibaldi, departed from Taranto on August 24 bound for Indonesia where it will be commissioned as KRI Gajah Mada. || President Prabowo visited earthquake-stricken East Nusa Tenggara on August 26 and asked survivors whether to continue the Free Nutritious Meals program.
